issue.title: [Bug]: Menu Bar Flashes
issue.body:
### Check existing issues

- [X] I have checked existing issues and believe that my issue is not a duplicate

### Description

Upon switching workspaces, the menu bar flashes as it appears to refresh. This is consistent w/ different methods to switch the workspace (i.e. swipe gestures/keybinds). It is present for both split and standard menu bars.

I am using Yabai, but the bug persists with it disabled.

### Steps to Reproduce

Switch workspaces and there's a flash.

### Ice Version

0.8.0

### macOS Version

14.4.1

### Screenshots


https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/assets/44217975/a48f3af0-af38-4035-ba36-03405c5412fc

comments.body: This is the expected behavior. macOS doesn't inform applications of workspace changes until after the change occurs. Ice moves the menu bar appearance overlay to the new space as soon as it receives the notification. We could theoretically maintain a separate overlay for each workspace, but that would waste lots of memory, as only one workspace can ever be visible per display.

> This is the expected behavior. macOS doesn't inform applications of workspace changes until after the change occurs. Ice moves the menu bar appearance overlay to the new space as soon as it receives the notification. We could theoretically maintain a separate overlay for each workspace, but that would waste lots of memory, as only one workspace can ever be visible per display.

Would it be possible to implement the solution and make it an optional setting that is set to false by default? Personally, the flashing is more important to me than my memory and maybe some other people have the same opinion.

- [ ] Create overlay for each workspace. (❔This will cause the menu bar to stop flashing but will also require more memory)

The text in brackets could be added as an information, visible as a tooltip when hovering over an info icon.

@rojnwa I recently implemented a mockup of this, and it doesn't seem like it actually would take much more memory. Seems like offscreen windows are pretty efficiently cached. So this is doable, I just need to get to it. #136 was opened recently, so I've been tracking the fix there.
@jordanbaird Great news! Looking forward to this but wouldn't it make more sense to flag #136 as duplicate and continue this one as it's older and essentially describes the same bug?
@rojnwa Yeah, you're probably right.

issue.title: [Bug]: Ice Bar doesn't reliably change color when activated on a new desktop
issue.body:
### Check existing and frequent issues

- [X] I have checked existing issues and believe that my issue is not a duplicate
- [X] I have read the [Frequent Issues](https://github.com/jordanbaird/Ice/blob/main/Documentation/FREQUENT_ISSUES.md) document, and my issue is not included there

### Description

When dragging the Ice Bar from one desktop to another, it doesn't update its color. This is expected, and is a workaround to ensure the Ice Bar's background matches the color of its icons (see #211).

issue.title: [Bug]: Menu bar shadow issue with single application window
issue.body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [x] I have checked existing issues, and this issue is not a duplicate

### Description

When enabling the `Shadow` option in Menu Bar Appearance, there's an inconsistent behavior in shadow rendering during window animations:

1. If the application has only **one** window open: The shadow moves downward along with the window animation when opening Application Windows
2. If the application has **more than one** window open: Shadow remains properly anchored during animations. Behaves as expected without positional shifts

---

**Expected Behavior:**
Shadow should remain positionally stable during animations regardless of the number of open windows, maintaining consistent visual appearance in both single and multi-window scenarios.







### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable "Shadow" in Ice preferences (Menu Bar Appearance)
2. Open an application (mine is Google Chrome) with only 1 window
3. Click `Show All Windows`
4. Observe shadow behavior during window opening animation
5. Repeat with an application that has 1+ windows

issue.title: [Feature Request]: Allow the tint option to affect the menubar background only and add transparency slider to colour swatch(es)
issue.body: ### Check Existing Issues - [x] I have checked existing issues, and this issue is not a duplicate ### Description The current “tint” option, under the Menu Bar Appearance section in Settings, affects the entirety of the menubar, including the Apple menu and other standard menu items, as well as the menu extras. This is undesirable behaviour, as it reduces contrast between the menu contents and its background. Also, this light tint, even if it did affect the background only, wouldn't offer as much contrast as entirely opaque or slightly transparent colours would. Adding a transparency slider for the single colour and the gradient swatches would allow for full control over the menubar's look, and having this layer disappear when triggering Mission Control would make for the most functionally optimal and aesthetically pleasing look. I am fully aware that these options might not work perfectly on setups with wildly varying desktop backgrounds across different displays and Mission Control spaces, but for micromanagers and perfectionists it could greatly enhance the experience of customizing one's desktop, especially after Apple's new Liquid Glass's gaussian blur effects started clashing in a very ugly fashion with custom menubar backgrounds embedded into desktop pictures (see screenshots), unlike in earlier macOS versions (Big Sur – Sequoia). ### Screenshots _No response_

comments.body:
There are certain features that require mouse tracking (show on hover being the main one). This can be optimized to not track the mouse if the features that need it are not enabled, though, so I'll keep this open.

Note that there will always be _some_ impact, even with optimization. Ice uses mouse events to handle menu bar item movement. Because of this, it needs to ensure that items are not moved while other mouse events are occurring, so tracking the mouse is required to some degree.

Second on this.

I really like Ice compared to other menu bar manager apps, especially since it's open source and has nice aesthetics throughout. However, Ice is by far the most power-hungry "background app" that I want to keep turned on all the time (Ice has an average 12-hour power of ~18 in Activity Monitor compared to low single digits of other background apps). I already switched off the separate "Use Ice Bar" feature because it was pushing 12-hour power into high 30s.

It is very insightful that you mentioned Ice uses mouse events to handle menu bar item movements. Is it possible to internally switching on/off tracking mouse events? For example, I have only the "Show on click" setting turned on. In this case, is it possible to only start tracking mouse events when the user has clicked on the menu bar?

Appreciate your great work!

comments.body:
Is it always at 15%? There are a couple cases I can think of that can temporarily raise the CPU load.

1. If you use the menu bar appearance feature, it's normal for CPU usage to increase temporarily after the focused app changes. The reason for this is that sometimes newly launched apps can take some time to populate their menus (Discord, for example starts with an empty menu, then adds the rest of its items after it finishes loading). To compensate for this, Ice polls for changes to the app menu's frame for a short time, which can temporarily cause this increase.
2. Mouse movement also causes an increase. If you've enabled features that require mouse tracking (such as showing hidden items on hover), there isn't much that can be done about this, as we have to compute whether the mouse is inside the menu bar whenever it moves. However, right now, some form of computation happens on mouse movement, regardless of what features are enabled. This can and should absolutely be optimized, so I'll keep this open for that purpose.

> Is it always at 15%? There are a couple cases I can think of that can temporarily raise the CPU load.
> 
> 1. If you use the menu bar appearance feature, it's normal for CPU usage to increase temporarily after the focused app changes. The reason for this is that sometimes newly launched apps can take some time to populate their menus (Discord, for example starts with an empty menu, then adds the rest of its items after it finishes loading). To compensate for this, Ice polls for changes to the app menu's frame for a short time, which can temporarily cause this increase.
> 2. Mouse movement also causes an increase. If you've enabled features that require mouse tracking (such as showing hidden items on hover), there isn't much that can be done about this, as we have to compute whether the mouse is inside the menu bar whenever it moves. However, right now, some form of computation happens on mouse movement, regardless of what features are enabled. This can and should absolutely be optimized, so I'll keep this open for that purpose.

Yes, the "appearance feature" is enabled. When I compared it with Bartender 5 (where the appearance feature is enabled), Bartender doesn't have this issue.
After consulting and comparing, I found there might be a potential "loophole" in ICE for your reference:
I launched iStat Menus (a monitoring tool for traffic, CPU, etc.), which displays real - time upload and download traffic in the menu bar. Does ICE trigger "polling" and "redraw" of the appearance when the traffic rate changes?
However, with Bartender 5, even with the appearance feature enabled and iStat Menus running, the traffic rate changes don't cause a CPU increase (it remains almost unchanged).

> Does ICE trigger "polling" and "redraw" of the appearance when the traffic rate changes?

Hmm, it shouldn't, unless the change in traffic rate causes some change in the menu bar. The traffic rate change could be triggering something else in the system that then in turn triggers Ice to poll or redraw.

When I first implemented the menu bar appearance feature, I tried using Accessibility to observe the menu bar instead of polling, but I couldn't get it to work reliably. It would honestly be the better way to handle menu bar changes, so I might try revisiting to see if I can get it to work. If not, I have a couple ideas to reduce the polling rate.
